content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate doughnut with chocolate icing is a soft, fried dough treat coated in a rich chocolate glaze. It combines a lightly sweet dough flavor with the deep taste of cocoa.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate doughnuts are a popular bakery item served alongside coffee.
The dough is traditionally leavened with yeast, giving the doughnut a light, airy texture.
The glaze can be made from dark, milk, or white chocolate depending on preference.
In some regions the doughnut is decorated with sprinkles, nuts, or caramel.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide quick energy, making the doughnut a convenient snack.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Cocoa in the chocolate glaze supplies iron, which is essential for hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate contains flavonoids that may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: If the dough is fried in partially hydrogenated oils, trans fats may be present, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergy
items.content: Doughnuts typically contain wheat flour and dairy, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Doughnuts are usually served warm and can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert or with coffee, tea, or milk. The glaze is eaten as‑is, and optional toppings like sprinkles or nuts can be added.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them and reheat in the oven before serving.
